diagnostic_evidence.quote: Our assumption is the minimal requirement to satisfy Stokes theorem in the proof of the main result
which are parallel to the boundary (i.e., the Lie algebra of $\hbox{Diff}_{\hbox{vol}}(\Omega))$

issues.failure_explanation: The standing Assumption requires the tangential component of $v$ to vanish on $\partial\Omega$ and calls this the minimal requirement for the boundary term in the proof to vanish. The boundary term in the divergence theorem is $\int_{\partial\Omega} k\,\delta v\cdot n\,dS$, which involves the normal component; a vanishing tangential component does not make it vanish. The paper's own Lie-algebra description (fields parallel to the boundary) and the later problem formulation (v vanishing entirely on $\partial\Omega$) use different, mutually inconsistent boundary conditions.

failure_location.quote: the tangencial component of $v$ vanishes at the boundary

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the Assumption by vanishing of the normal component $v\cdot n$ on $\partial\Omega$ (or state full vanishing consistently) and drop or correct the minimality remark.
issues.overall_effect: The stated Assumption does not support the boundary-term cancellation in the proof of Theorem 1; the proof actually relies on the stronger condition (full vanishing of $v$) imposed in the definition of $\mathcal{C}$, so the claim about minimality of the assumption is false.
issues.title: Boundary assumption (vanishing tangential component) is the wrong condition for the divergence-theorem step
issues.why_classification: A local restatement of the boundary condition fixes the inconsistency; the proof already uses the stronger condition and no result is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Each $\varphi\in\hbox{Diff}_{\hbox{vol}}(\Omega)$ is a map from $\Omega$ to $\Omega$
This ensures that  such an optimal trajectory does not intersect $S$.
The pressure $p$ is determined by the divergence-free (volume-preserving) constraint $\hbox{div}\,v=0$.
imposing an artificial potential in the fluid context is equivalent to generating a desired pressure

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims that adding $\int_\Omega V\circ\varphi$ to the cost yields obstacle avoidance and 'modified' fluid dynamics. But every admissible $\varphi(\cdot,t)$ is a volume-preserving diffeomorphism of $\Omega$ onto $\Omega$, so by the paper's own identity (change:variables) with $b\equiv 1$, $\int_\Omega V\circ\varphi\,dX=\int_\Omega V\,dx$ is independent of $\varphi$: the cost differs from the classical one of bloch2000optimal by a constant, and the minimizers are unchanged. Consistently, the derived equation (mod:eulereq) is the Euler equation with pressure $p-V$; since the pressure is determined by $\hbox{div}\,v=0$, the velocity field is identical to that of the unmodified Euler equations and $V$ has no effect on the flow. Moreover, since $\varphi$ is onto $\Omega\supset S$, fluid particles always occupy $S$, so 'the optimal trajectory does not intersect $S$' is false; with $V=\tau/(|x-a|^2-r^2)$ the integrand is non-integrably singular (of both signs) on and inside the sphere, so the functional is not even well defined.

failure_location.quote: Here $V$ denotes a potential function used to avoid certain region in $\Omega$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must reformulate the problem so that the potential term is not invariant under volume-preserving relabelling (e.g., a different configuration space, non-onto maps, or a cost not absorbable into the pressure) and withdraw the obstacle-avoidance claims for the present formulation.
issues.overall_effect: The central advertised contribution (obstacle avoidance for fluid particles via an artificial potential, 'modified Euler equations' distinct from Euler's) is unsupported: Theorems 1–2 are consistent but reduce to the classical necessary conditions with a relabelled pressure, and the remark's avoidance guarantee is false. The simulated influence of $V$ on the velocity cannot reflect the continuous system.
issues.title: Potential term is constant on volume-preserving maps: obstacle avoidance is vacuous and V only shifts the pressure
issues.why_classification: The primary claim of the paper (obstacle avoidance through the potential, and dynamics differing from Euler's) has no surviving comparable version in the stated setting; a new formulation would be required.

issues.failure_explanation: The functional $\mathcal{J}$ carries $-\tfrac12\langle v,v\rangle$ but $+\langle V\circ\varphi\rangle$, so it is not (up to sign) the Hamilton–Pontryagin extension of the cost in (first:functional), which has both terms with the same sign. Moreover the proof's last step is an invalid inference: from $(Tv\circ\varphi)^T\pi+\partial_t\pi+\hbox{grad}V\circ\varphi=0$ one gets $\partial_t\pi=-(Tv\circ\varphi)^T\pi-\hbox{grad}V\circ\varphi$, not $+\hbox{grad}V\circ\varphi$. Hence critical points of $\mathcal{J}$ as defined do not satisfy (necessary:conditions), and following the proof of Theorem 2 they satisfy $\partial_t v+v\cdot\hbox{grad}v=-\hbox{grad}(p+V)$ rather than $-\hbox{grad}(p-V)$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define $\mathcal{J}$ with consistent signs, e.g. $\langle\pi,v\circ\varphi-\partial_t\varphi\rangle-\tfrac12\langle v,v\rangle-\langle k\,\hbox{div}\,v+V\circ\varphi\rangle$, and correct the sign of the $\langle\hbox{grad}V\circ\varphi,\delta\varphi\rangle$ term in the variation; then the stated equations follow.
issues.overall_effect: Theorems 1 and 2 are false as stated for the functional $\mathcal{J}$ actually defined; the sign of the potential term in (necessary:conditions) and (mod:eulereq) is reversed relative to $\mathcal{J}$.
issues.title: Sign inconsistency between the functional $\mathcal{J}$ and the derived adjoint equation
issues.why_classification: A local sign correction in the definition of $\mathcal{J}$ and one line of the proof restores both theorems exactly as stated.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: be an arbitrary smooth variation of the point $(\varphi, v, \pi, k)$ on $\mathcal{C}$

issues.failure_explanation: The space $\mathcal{C}$ requires $\varphi(\cdot,t)\in\hbox{Diff}_{\hbox{vol}}(\Omega)$, so admissible variations have the form $\delta\varphi=\xi\circ\varphi$ with $\xi$ divergence-free and tangent to $\partial\Omega$; they are not arbitrary. The fundamental lemma then only yields that $(Tv\circ\varphi)^T\pi+\partial_t\pi+\hbox{grad}V\circ\varphi$ is $L^2$-orthogonal to such fields, i.e. equals $(\hbox{grad}\lambda)\circ\varphi$ for some scalar $\lambda$, not zero. The pointwise adjoint equation in (necessary:conditions) is therefore not established as written.

failure_location.quote: Thus, again by the fundamental theorem of calculus of variations, we conclude that

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Drop the requirement $\varphi(\cdot,t)\in\hbox{Diff}_{\hbox{vol}}(\Omega)$ from $\mathcal{C}$ (volume preservation follows at critical points from $\partial_t\varphi=v\circ\varphi$, $\hbox{div}\,v=0$ and $\varphi_0\in\hbox{Diff}_{\hbox{vol}}$), so variations $\delta\varphi$ are unconstrained and (change:variables) applies at the critical point; or state the equation modulo a gradient.
issues.overall_effect: The third equation of (necessary:conditions) is proved only modulo a gradient term; Theorem 2 is unaffected since such a term is absorbed into the pressure.
issues.title: Fundamental lemma applied to constrained variations $\delta\varphi$ tangent to Diff_vol
issues.why_classification: A short redefinition of the admissible class (or a gauge remark) restores the stated conclusion without changing any result.

issues.failure_explanation: For $u=-\sin y\cos x$, $v=\sin y\cos x$ one has $\partial_x u+\partial_y v=\sin x\sin y+\cos x\cos y=\cos(x-y)\neq 0$, so the initial data violate the constraint $\hbox{div}\,v=0$, contradicting the claim that the simulation starts from divergence-free initial conditions.

failure_location.quote: even though we depart from divergence-free initial conditions

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use divergence-free initial data (e.g. $u=\sin x\cos y$, $v=-\cos x\sin y$) or state that the initial field is first Helmholtz-projected.
issues.overall_effect: The simulation does not start on the constraint set of (mod:eulereq); the interpretation of the divergence produced during integration is unreliable.
issues.title: Stated initial velocity field is not divergence-free
issues.why_classification: A local change of the initial data (or an explicit initial projection) removes the contradiction without affecting any theoretical claim.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: First, we used finite differences to approximate the solution of the first equation in \eqref{mod:eulereq}

issues.failure_explanation: The scheme integrates only the first equation of (mod:eulereq) for 140 steps and applies the discrete Helmholtz projection a single time afterwards. No procedure for computing the pressure $p$ (which in the continuous system is determined by $\hbox{div}\,v=0$ at every instant) is given, and the divergence constraint is not enforced during the time stepping. A single terminal projection of an unconstrained trajectory is not an approximation of the constrained flow; in particular, because $-\hbox{grad}(p-V)$ is a pure gradient that the pressure absorbs, any visible effect of $V$ on the projected velocity is an artifact of omitting $p$ during integration.

failure_location.quote: Therefore, after the time integration stage is completed we projected our solution to a divergence free-vector field using the approach explained in the previous section.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a projection method that enforces the discrete divergence constraint (solving the discrete Poisson equation for the pressure) at every time step, and specify how $p$ is treated.
issues.overall_effect: The reported simulation results do not approximate solutions of (mod:eulereq) and cannot support the qualitative claims about the fluid's behaviour near the obstacle.
issues.title: Time-stepping scheme ignores the pressure/incompressibility constraint and projects only once at the end
issues.why_classification: Repair requires a contained but nontrivial change to the numerical procedure (per-step pressure projection), not a one-line fix, while the theoretical results are untouched.
